correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the full all-integer argument from actual Git RESULT.md at source commit and independent code. For G=K_m square P_n, m>=3,n>=4, Euclidean Q=B^T(BB^T)^+B and P=I-Q, the product Laplacian splits into uniform-clique L_path and orthogonal-clique (mI+L_path) blocks. Positive Green matrices R=(mI+L_path)^{-1} and E=(mI+D_path^T D_path)^{-1} yield the four exact cut/cycle column families H_x, Hprime_x, V_j, Vprime_j; dipole sign/flux identities justify their absolute column sums. The tridiagonal recurrence verifies image-formula endpoint kernels in rho. Balancing rho powers locates their central orbit maxima. The source inequality bounding clique cut columns by 2(m-1)/m+4/sqrt(m(m+4)), checked with u=rho^x, v=rho^(n-1-x), is strictly beaten by central path cut columns for all allowed m,n via n=4 base and Green monotonicity. For cycle columns, check the m=3 n=4 and n>=5 comparisons and m=4/ m>=5 polynomial inequalities, then extend in n by positivity; switch at m=4 is strict. Norm-ordering follows from 2(m-1)E_jj-1>0 for m>=4 and two strict rho parity inequalities at m=3. Actual hypotheses, equality/strictness, normalization, edge orientations and complementary cycle projection are explicit. Independently recomputed 286 (m,n) reduced cases with exact rational finite Green matrices and 1029 complete full-graph edge columns across ten graphs (2058 induced column-norm checks); these are finite corroborations, not an infinite proof. No substantive contradiction found in the uniform argument.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge independent comparison of the mathematical claim, not its title: the paper establishes exact induced edge-ell_1 norms of BOTH specific canonical Euclidean cut/cycle projections on K_m square P_n for all m>=3, n>=4, plus maximizing edge orbit and strict parity/clique-width switch. The 2023 graph cycle-space projection paper contains the same general operator framework but its substantive family results address tori, Hamming graphs and invariant/minimal projections; the 2018 finite Lipschitz-free-space paper supplies quotient machinery; the 2026 electrical-flow localization paper explicitly uses the transfer-current projector BL^+B^T but establishes average or spectral upper bounds, not these exact max-column formulas. Actual Resultary searches returned cactus coordinate-basis and clustered-metric projections, which differ in both underlying objects and operators. Unindexed equivalent transfer-current formulae remain an explicitly documented risk.

value.rationale: This is a complete explicit two-parameter operator-norm classification of a natural connected graph-product family and its canonical cut/cycle splitting, not an arbitrary tiny instance. The m=3 parity reversal in ||Q|| versus ||P|| for all path lengths and the sharp m=4 maximizing-edge-orbit transition encode nontrivial effects of open boundaries and clique width. Exact max-current amplification of these canonical projectors is a motivated invariant for electrical/graph cycle-space analysis and a precise benchmark for product-graph Banach-space decompositions. All m>=3,n>=4 are covered by the symbolic Green proof and the new strict cases are not trivially inferred from broad projection bounds. Correctness, executable checker availability and novelty searches alone are not the value rationale. Does not assert minimality among all projections or weighted/general product cases.

limitations: Finite calculations are supporting consistency checks only; infinite parameter claims rely on the complete tridiagonal-Green and inequality proof.
Only real, connected unit-weight clique-path graphs K_m square P_n (integers m>=3,n>=4), canonical Euclidean orthogonal projections and induced ell_1 (equiv ell_infinity by symmetry) norms.
Does not establish minimality among all projections, or extensions to arbitrary weights or other product graph families.
Best-of-knowledge originality is qualified by less-indexed transfer-current tables and incomplete historical coverage; specific inspected literature is listed.
